units.text: 苹果正在将人工智能进一步整合到旗下办公与创作软件中，为Pages文字处理软件、Keynote演示文稿工具和Numbers电子表格应用加入全新的AI助手。用户可以通过自然语言指令，让AI根据现有文档理解上下文、起草和修改文字、制作幻灯片、生成公式以及整理数据。这项更新标志着苹果正尝试将AI从系统级功能延伸至日常办公流程。
这款名为“智能助手”（Intelligent Assistant）的功能由苹果与OpenAI的人工智能模型提供支持。它并非只负责回答问题，而是能够结合用户当前正在编辑的文档或表格执行任务，帮助用户直接完成内容创作和修改。
在Pages中，智能助手能够根据用户的要求起草文章、重新组织段落、调整写作语气，并对现有内容进行编辑和润色。用户也可以让它撰写特定章节，生成图片或图形元素，或者查询某个主题的最新信息，再将相关内容整合进文档中。
对于不熟悉Pages高级功能的用户，助手还可以提供操作指导，解释如何使用特定工具，并根据当前文档提出改进建议。相比单纯在独立聊天窗口中询问AI，直接在文档环境中工作，有望减少复制粘贴和反复切换应用的操作。
Keynote的智能助手则主要面向演示文稿制作。用户可以要求AI根据主题构建演示内容、生成幻灯片、编写演讲者备注、添加动画，并对已有页面进行调整和完善。助手还可以生成图片与图形元素，帮助用户更快地建立演示文稿的视觉结构。
这一功能可能对需要频繁制作商业报告、教学课件和项目汇报的用户尤其有用。传统演示文稿制作不仅需要整理信息，还涉及页面布局、视觉设计和叙事结构。AI助手试图将这些步骤整合到同一工作流程中，让用户能够通过文字描述表达目标，再由软件协助完成具体操作。
在Numbers中，智能助手能够根据表格内容寻找数据规律、生成复杂公式、建立自定义表格，并推荐适合的数据可视化图表。用户可以使用自然语言描述计算需求，而不必完全依赖对电子表格函数的熟悉程度。
例如，用户可以要求软件分析某组数据的变化趋势、创建汇总表，或者生成能够完成特定计算的公式。对于需要处理大量数据但不具备专业数据分析技能的用户，这类功能有望降低使用门槛。不过，AI生成的公式和分析结果仍需要核对，尤其是在财务计算、业务决策等对准确性要求较高的场景中。
此次更新还有一项重要变化：苹果开始允许第三方AI智能体接入旗下办公应用。Pages、Keynote和Numbers在macOS 27及更新版本中支持模型上下文协议（Model Context Protocol，MCP），使符合条件的第三方AI智能体能够与这些应用进行交互。
MCP是一种用于连接AI模型与外部工具、数据源及应用程序的开放协议。它可以让AI不再局限于生成文本，而是根据授权访问相应工具，并执行更具体的工作流程。对于办公软件而言，这意味着未来用户可能通过不同的AI助手操作文档、演示文稿和电子表格，而不必完全依赖苹果内置的智能助手。
智能助手目前以测试版形式推出，适用于支持Apple Intelligence的设备，需要运行iOS 27、iPadOS 27或macOS 27及更新版本。相关功能的可用范围还受到语言和订阅条件限制，现阶段并非所有用户都能直接使用完整功能。
除了办公软件，苹果也为其他创作应用带来了人工智能升级。Pixelmator Pro新增“生成式填充”（Generate Fill）功能，用户可以通过文字描述修改图片中的特定区域。系统会尝试匹配周围环境的光线、透视关系和纹理，使修改后的内容更自然地融入原图。
这一功能有望简化以往需要通过复杂选区、图层和修图工具才能完成的操作。用户可以描述希望添加、删除或改变的内容，再由AI生成相应结果。不过，生成效果仍取决于图像内容、提示词以及模型对场景的理解程度。
Logic Pro for Mac和iPad也将迎来采用Liquid Glass视觉风格的界面调整，并加入AI助手。苹果表示，用户可以通过一次提示创建人声录音轨道的基础设置，也可以让助手协助修改已有音乐项目。Mac版Logic Pro还将重新设计浏览器，并利用设备端人工智能自动分析、分类和标记导入的声音素材。
对于音乐制作人员而言，素材整理往往需要耗费大量时间。自动识别声音类型并添加标签，有望让用户更快找到合适的音效和录音片段，而AI辅助轨道设置则可能降低部分制作流程的操作复杂度。
苹果还计划更新Final Cut Pro视频编辑软件，将MotionVFX提供的模板、图形、标题和转场效果直接整合进应用。Final Cut Pro也将内置Content Hub，提供可供创作者使用的素材库，其中包括库存视频、照片和背景等内容。
苹果表示，上述创作应用更新将于11月向现有Creator Studio订阅用户免费提供。
从整体方向来看，苹果正在尝试将人工智能从单独的聊天界面转变为嵌入式生产力工具。无论是修改文章、制作演示文稿、分析表格，还是整理音乐素材，AI都开始直接参与用户正在进行的工作，而不再只是提供文字建议。
不过，AI助手能否真正提高工作效率，仍取决于生成内容的准确性、用户对结果的控制能力，以及不同应用之间的协作程度。尤其是在复杂文档、财务数据和专业创作任务中，人工智能仍可能产生错误或不符合预期的结果，用户依然需要检查和调整。
对于苹果而言，这轮更新不仅是为现有软件增加新功能，也是在回应微软、Google等竞争对手持续将AI整合进办公产品的趋势。随着自然语言操作和第三方AI智能体逐步进入生产力软件，未来办公应用的竞争重点，可能从单纯提供编辑工具，转向能否理解用户意图并协助完成完整任务。

units.text: Apple has launched an updated iMac for the first time since 2024, bringing this longstanding favorite up to the speeds of the latest Mac mini.
If it ain't broke, eventually update it. Apple has released its first update to the all-in-one iMac since the 2024 edition gained an M4 processor.

"iMac is the world's best all-in-one, and today it raises the bar yet again," said Shelly Goldberg, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering in a statement. "With the blazing performance and AI capabilities of M6 supercharging every workflow and the next generation of Apple Intelligence with Siri AI — combined with its stunning 24-inch Retina display, its gorgeous design in seven vibrant colors, and macOS 27 — the new iMac has everything users need to run their businesses, manage their lives, and bring their ideas to life."

Announced ahead of the "Pro and Tell" event that's due to feature the revised MacBook Pro, this iMac release is the next to get a new generation of Apple Silicon. As previously expected, there's been no major redesign to the chassis, which remains as it has been since 2020.
That chassis comes in the same seven colors as the previous edition:
Blue
Green
Pink
Yellow
Purple
Orange
Silver
There have been a series of upgrades to the iMac's connectivity, though. It now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, plus Apple says its storage is up to twice as fast as the previous model.
The new iMac with M6 comes in two main configurations:
10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, two Thunderbolt ports, from $1,499
12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, four Thunderbolt ports, 2.5 gigabit Ethernet, from $1,699
In the former, the 10-core CPU has two super cores, three performance cores, and five efficiency ones. The latter 12-core CPU has two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency ones.
Both versions start with 16GB RAM and 256GB storage. The base 10-core version can be upgraded to 24GB RAM, while the 12-core edition can go to 24GB or 32GB RAM.
That base model can be upgraded to 512GB storage or 1TB. The 12-core version can also go to 2TB storage.
By default, the 10-core edition does not come with Ethernet at all, but it can be configured with 2.5 gigabit Ethernet for $30. The 12-core version has 2.5 gigabit Ethernet as standard.
To upgrade or not
So an outside observer wouldn't notice any difference, but a user would. The jump from M4 to M6 is not as great as when the iMac went from Intel to Apple Silicon, but it is still noticeable.
It's arguable whether it's noticeable enough to be worth upgrading from the M4 edition. But that will become clearer once this iMac can be tested.
Users of the 2023 M3 edition will of course see more of an improvement. But this iMac is really aimed primarily at the remaining Intel Mac users, plus perhaps those on the original M1 Apple Silicon.

Apple says that typical uses such as photo editing are twice as fast as before, though. Overall AI computing speed has doubled, too, because of the dual 16-core Neural Engine, plus higher memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s.
Specifically for AI prompt processing in LM Studio, Apple says that the M6 iMac is five times faster than the previous M4 model. It's up to 12 times faster than the M1 iMac.
The new M6 iMac starts at $1,499. Pre-orders open on October 28, 2026, and it will ship on November 6.

evidence.discovery_lead: tvOS 27.2 was released on Monday for the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer, but the Apple TV does not show release notes for software updates in the Settings app. Instead, Apple periodically updates a support document outlining what is new in tvOS updates, and the release notes for tvOS 27.2 are now available. Note that Apple never released a tvOS 27.1 version, so tvOS 27.2 is the first Apple TV software update since tvOS 27 was released in September. Apple says tvOS 27.2 includes a few FaceTime enhancements, plus the ability to shuffle through different screen saver categories. In addition, the Find My app now supports the Siri Remote (2nd generation) and later, but Precision Finding is limited to the Siri Remote (4th generation). The update also contains bug fixes and security patches. Here are Apple's full tvOS 27.2 release notes: This update brings new ways to stay connected with FaceTime, personalize your screen saver, and locate your Siri Remote with Find My, along with bug fixes and security updates for your Apple TV 4K. FaceTime FaceTime links make it easier to join calls directly from your Apple TV.
evidence.discovery_title: Apple Shares tvOS 27.2 Release Notes With List of New Features

tvOS 27.2 was released on Monday for the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer, but the Apple TV does not show release notes for software updates in the Settings app. Instead, Apple periodically updates a support document outlining what is new in tvOS updates, and the release notes for tvOS 27.2 are now available.
Note that Apple never released a tvOS 27.1 version, so tvOS 27.2 is the first Apple TV software update since tvOS 27 was released in September.

Apple says tvOS 27.2 includes a few FaceTime enhancements, plus the ability to shuffle through different screen saver categories. In addition, the Find My app now supports the Siri Remote (2nd generation) and later, but Precision Finding is limited to the Siri Remote (4th generation). The update also contains bug fixes and security patches.
Here are Apple's full tvOS 27.2 release notes:
This update brings new ways to stay connected with FaceTime, personalize your screen saver, and locate your Siri Remote with Find My, along with bug fixes and security updates for your Apple TV 4K.
FaceTime
FaceTime links make it easier to join calls directly from your Apple TV.
Sign language interpreter and captioning support lets you add third-party services to your calls.
Screen Savers
Photo personalization lets you use your iPhone to choose specific photos for your screen saver without sharing your full library with Apple TV.
Shuffle option lets you enjoy different screen saver categories as your Apple TV cycles through them.
Find My
Find My support lets you locate your Siri Remote (2nd generation) or later using your iPhone.

Apple said Siri AI will be available on the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer, but this functionality is not yet enabled on these models on tvOS 27.2. The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) launches on Friday, November 13, and Siri AI is one of its headline new features, so perhaps the feature will come to older models closer to then.

units.text: Today Apple introduced a new iMac with the M6 chip, combining powerful performance upgrades with a couple other improvements.
Apple announces M6 iMac with faster chip, N1 wireless upgrades, improved Ethernet
Apple is in the midst of a week of product unveilings. Yesterday brought the new iPad mini with OLED, and now today there’s an upgraded iMac powered by the M6 chip.
The new iMac has the same 24-inch display and overall design as before, but with upgraded internals.

M6 is the main focus here, with notable improvements over the M4 model in several key areas. It has an up to 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. The previous iMac only offered up to a 10-core CPU and GPU, and 16-core Neural Engine.
Compared to M4, users should expect up to:
40% faster CPU performance
2x faster graphics
2x faster storage
5x faster on-device AI performance
View all comments
Additional new features of the iMac include:
N1 wireless chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, up from Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3
configurable with 2.5Gb Ethernet for “up to 2.5x faster wired connectivity than the previous generation”
Up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth (previously 120GB/s)
The M6 iMac starts at $1,499, the same price as before.
Pre-orders for the new iMac start tomorrow, October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT. That’s expected to be just minutes after the rumored MacBook Pro redesign is unveiled. It will ship Friday, November 6.
*Buy Mac with 15% discount from Apple refurbished

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技10月28日消息，苹果又给iPhone加入了一项新功能， 苹果在iOS 27.2中新增自拍年龄验证方式，用户在需要确认是否成年的场景下，可以通过自拍让系统估算年龄，不一定非要掏出身份证或使用信用卡验证。 据了解，随着越来越多国家和地区要求对用户进行年龄验证，iPhone用户在创建Apple账户、更新系统、下载应用或调整部分设置时，都可能需要先确认自己是否成年。 据9to5Mac报道，目前，澳大利亚、巴西、新加坡、韩国、英国以及美国得克萨斯州等地区，已在部分场景中实施相关年龄验证要求。 此前，苹果已支持信用卡验证、扫描身份证件等方式，此次iOS 27.2又增加了自拍选项，相当于给用户提供了另一种选择。 具体操作也不复杂， 用户选择自拍验证后，需要将面部对准取景框，再按照屏幕提示缓慢向右、向左、向上和向下转动头部，完成四个方向的面部采集。 随后，系统会通过年龄估算模型分析面部图像，判断用户是否达到成年年龄。 隐私方面，苹果表示，年龄估算模型会在设备本地和私有云计算环境中运行。 自拍图像不会向任何人开放，包括苹果自身， 在完成年龄确认后，相关自拍照片会立即删除，不会以任何形式留存。 快科技10月28日消息，苹果又给iPhone加入了一项新功能，苹果在iOS 27.2中新增自拍年龄验证方式，用户在需要确认是否成年的场景下，可以通过自拍让系统估算年龄，不一定非要掏出身份证或使用信用

evidence.title: 约翰·特努斯预告触屏MacBook Pro：OLED屏幕、全新铰链与灵动岛设计即将登场

units.text: 苹果首席执行官约翰·特努斯于当地时间10月28日在社交媒体发布了一段简短的预热视频，画面显示苹果标志投射在夜间城市天际线背景下的深色墙壁上。虽然视频没有直接展示任何新产品，也没有明确提及触摸屏，但由于苹果预计当天公布搭载OLED触摸屏的新款MacBook Pro，这段视频被普遍视为新产品发布前的预热。
苹果已经邀请部分科技媒体记者和内容创作者前往洛杉矶，参加名为“Pro and tell”的产品体验活动。活动预计于当地时间上午10时举行，受邀者有望现场体验苹果首款触屏MacBook，以及新款iPad mini、iMac和本周早些时候公布的14英寸MacBook Pro等产品。
如果相关传闻最终得到证实，苹果将首次在MacBook产品线上引入原生触摸屏，结束公司长期以来对笔记本电脑触控操作持保留态度的传统。
根据目前流传的消息，新款触屏MacBook Pro预计提供14英寸和16英寸两种尺寸，并采用OLED显示屏。与现有MacBook Pro使用的Mini-LED或LCD技术相比，OLED能够让像素独立发光，在显示黑色时关闭相应像素，因此可以提供更高的对比度、更鲜艳的色彩以及更好的暗部表现。新屏幕的峰值亮度也有望得到提升。
触摸屏将与传统键盘和触控板同时保留，用户可以根据具体任务选择操作方式。苹果预计不会将MacBook简单改造成一台放大版iPad，而是继续以完整的macOS系统为基础，针对触控操作增加相应的软件优化。
这一设计方向也意味着，触屏MacBook与iPad之间的界限可能进一步模糊，但两类设备仍将保留不同的产品定位。MacBook继续强调桌面级应用、多窗口工作流程和传统输入方式，而触摸屏则为用户提供直接操作屏幕内容的另一种选择。
为了避免用户触摸屏幕时整块显示面板明显晃动，新款MacBook Pro据称将采用经过重新设计、支撑力度更强的铰链。笔记本电脑的屏幕与底座之间通过铰链连接，触摸屏幕时产生的压力会传递到这一结构。如果铰链阻尼和支撑力度不足，屏幕就容易随手指动作前后摆动，影响操作体验。
据称，新款产品还将重新设计散热系统，改善气流通过铰链区域的方式。由于高性能处理器在运行大型应用和复杂计算任务时会产生大量热量，苹果需要在更薄的机身、更轻的重量与散热能力之间取得平衡。新的铰链和散热结构是否会带来明显的性能或噪声改善，仍有待实际测试。
外观方面，新款机型预计会进一步缩窄屏幕边框，并采用类似iPhone的灵动岛设计，取代目前MacBook Pro屏幕顶部的传统刘海。灵动岛有望用于显示系统通知、后台活动和其他实时信息，让摄像头区域与软件界面形成更紧密的结合。
机身也预计会变得更薄、更轻。对于需要经常携带笔记本电脑的专业用户而言，这可能改善移动办公体验。不过，苹果如何在减轻重量的同时维持机身刚性、电池续航和散热能力，将成为新设计需要面对的实际考验。
性能方面，传闻称这批触屏MacBook Pro可能继续采用现有的M5 Pro和M5 Max芯片，而不是同步升级至更新一代的专业级处理器。这意味着，购买者获得的主要升级可能集中在显示屏、触控交互和机身设计上，而非处理器性能的大幅提升。
软件方面，新机预计将运行针对触摸操作进行优化的macOS Golden Gate。系统可能加入更适合手指操作的控件、菜单和交互方式，以减少传统桌面界面在触屏设备上的操作不便。苹果需要解决的关键问题是，如何让触摸操作自然地融入现有macOS工作流程，同时避免影响键盘和触控板用户的使用习惯。
价格方面，MacRumors汇总的传闻显示，美国市场14英寸触屏机型的起售价预计不低于2899美元，16英寸机型则可能不低于3399美元。若最终定价接近这些水平，触屏版本将明显定位于高端专业市场，而不是取代现有MacBook Pro成为所有用户的标准选择。上述价格目前仍属于发布前传闻，并非苹果正式公布的售价。
苹果长期以来对笔记本电脑触摸屏保持谨慎态度。已故苹果联合创始人史蒂夫·乔布斯曾在2010年表示，将触摸屏直接用于传统笔记本电脑在人体工学方面存在问题；时任首席执行官Tim Cook也曾质疑，将不同类型设备强行合并是否有意义。苹果此前一直通过iPad提供触控计算体验，同时坚持MacBook采用键盘和触控板为主的操作方式。
然而，触摸屏笔记本电脑在Windows生态中已经发展多年，消费者对不同设备之间操作方式一致性的期待也在变化。随着苹果进一步完善iPad和Mac的软件能力，公司可能正在重新评估触控操作在传统电脑上的价值。
触屏MacBook能否获得用户认可，最终仍取决于实际体验。OLED屏幕可以改善画质，触控功能也能为部分创作和浏览任务提供便利，但如果用户仍需要频繁抬起手臂触摸竖直屏幕，或者macOS的软件界面没有针对手指操作进行充分优化，那么新功能未必能够显著提升工作效率。
苹果预计将在当天的产品体验活动中展示更多细节。随着触屏MacBook Pro即将亮相，市场关注的焦点已经从苹果是否会推出触摸屏笔记本电脑，转向公司将如何整合硬件、操作系统和传统电脑使用习惯，打造不同于现有Windows触屏笔记本的产品体验。

units.text: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，市场研究机构 Counterpoint Research 的《智能手机周度销量追踪报告》显示，苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 系列 9 月上市三周，全球销量较去年同期的 iPhone 17 Pro 系列增长 3.1%。
从各地区表现来看，增长主要由中国市场拉动。iPhone 18 Pro 系列在中国的销量同比大涨 29%，得益于上市初期供货比去年充足，以及中国安卓手机厂商的竞品旗舰机型涨价。如果没有中国市场的贡献，全球销量增幅将远低于 3.1%。
美国和日本市场则出现同比下滑，主要受到新机涨价的影响。美国消费者普遍认为，新机在功能和设计方面相比上一代没有明显提升；日本则因汇率变化放大了价格涨幅，导致需求减少。
IT之家从报告中获悉，iPhone 18 Pro Max 占整个 Pro 系列销量的 56%，略低于去年的 57%。除了新机价格上涨，印度、东南亚等新兴市场的销量增长更多来自 Pro 机型，也是 Pro Max 销量占比下降的原因。
Counterpoint Research 副总监林秀晶指出：“中国市场的强劲表现能否持续，还是因为消费者提前集中购机，未来几周就会更加清楚。美国和日本市场的销量能否回升，以及第 34 周上市的 iPhone Duo 究竟会带来新的购买需求，还是分流 Pro Max 的销量，是短期内最值得关注的两个因素。”

研究总监塔伦 · 帕塔克指出：“iPhone 18 Pro 系列在不同市场的反响有好有坏。我们每周都在追踪销量，观察上市初期的销售高峰过去后，需求还能保持多久。这将影响年末购物季的销售表现。去年 iPhone 17 系列卖得非常好，但存储成本上涨带来的涨价压力，以及宏观经济的不确定性，都在影响消费者换机。整体来看，换机周期越来越长。不过，即使销量增幅只有个位数，对苹果仍然有利：更多消费者换购 Pro 系列，有助于改善营收结构。此外，iPhone Duo 的预订表现也很强劲，当前供不应求。”

units.text: Apple’s Director of European Government Affairs, Sébastien Gros, will speak at this year’s Web Summit in Lisbon, Portugal, taking place November 9–12. Here are the details.
Apple to return to Web Summit
Over the past few years, Apple has regularly sent executives to speak at Web Summit.

From Craig Federighi, who argued against allowing sideloading on the iPhone in 2021, to Sumbul Desai discussing Apple’s healthcare initiatives in 2022, to Sarah Herrlinger exploring accessibility and AI in 2024, to Apple Music co-lead Ole Obermann discussing the music industry in 2025, Apple has used the event to address a wide range of topics.
This year, as spotted by iFeed, the company will send Sébastien Gros, its Director of Government Affairs for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA), to speak at the event.
As of now, details about Gros’s participation, including the subject of his session, have not yet been announced.

As is usually the case, this year’s Web Summit is shaping up to be a massive gathering, with more than 850 speakers (including a few humanoid robots) from dozens of countries and territories, representing hundreds of companies alongside universities, public institutions and other organizations.
For those following Apple, another notable speaker on this year’s lineup is Tony Fadell, the former Apple executive who helped create the iPod and iPhone.
To learn more about this year’s Web Summit, follow this link.

evidence.title: iPhone Duo铰链供应商否认质量问题 称屏幕破裂原因尚未查明

units.text: 苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 上市后接连出现内屏破裂报告，部分用户和拆解人员将怀疑焦点指向设备的铰链机构。面对持续发酵的舆论，苹果供应链企业 Fine M-Tec 于10月26日发表声明，否认其供应的组件存在导致屏幕损坏的质量缺陷，并呼吁外界在真正原因查明之前，不要急于认定责任方。
据韩国科技媒体《The Elec》报道，Fine M-Tec 在声明中表示，近期部分产品出现的质量问题，并非由该公司供应的组件缺陷造成。尽管声明没有直接点名苹果或 iPhone Duo，但发布时间恰逢这款折叠屏手机出现铰链及内屏故障争议，因此被视为对相关质疑的回应。
Fine M-Tec 是一家生产折叠屏设备内部铰链及金属支撑板的企业。此类组件主要用于支撑柔性OLED显示屏，帮助屏幕在反复折叠和展开时承受机械应力。该公司也是三星显示相关供应链中的零部件供应商，在折叠屏手机产业链中具有一定业务基础。
此次争议源于 iPhone Duo 上市后出现的多起屏幕损坏报告。部分用户表示，设备在正常展开过程中突然出现异常阻力，随后传出清晰的断裂声，内屏则出现从中央折痕向一侧延伸的横向亮线或其他显示异常。部分案例发生在购买后不久，甚至在使用数小时后便出现故障。
由于不同用户报告的损坏位置较为相似，外界开始怀疑问题可能并非单纯的柔性屏幕材料缺陷，而是与铰链内部某个机械部件的失效有关。
此前，YouTube创作者 CuriousHagi 拆解了一台发生故障的 iPhone Duo，并在铰链内部发现一个已经断裂的金属部件。该部件位于屏幕中央附近，尺寸和厚度与周围结构有所不同。拆解过程中还发现，相关区域存在疑似机械部件相互挤压或接触留下的痕迹。
一种可能的解释是，铰链内部的某个部件在折叠过程中发生错位或卡滞，继而承受过大的机械应力并断裂。断裂后的金属部件可能进一步接触屏幕背面，使柔性显示面板局部受力集中，最终造成显示损坏。不过，这仍属于根据个别损坏设备提出的推测，尚不能证明所有发生故障的 iPhone Duo 都由相同原因引发。
Fine M-Tec 不仅否认自身供应的零部件存在缺陷，还表示正在考虑对未经验证便指称其组件存在问题的相关人士采取法律行动。该公司显然希望避免在调查结果尚未明确时，供应商被舆论直接认定为事故责任方。
从技术角度看，折叠屏手机的铰链并非简单的转轴，而是由多个精密部件组成的机械系统，需要在有限空间内协调屏幕弯曲、支撑结构移动以及排线变形等过程。任何一个部件出现尺寸偏差、装配问题或异常磨损，都可能影响整个机构的运行。因此，即使损坏位置集中在铰链附近，也不能仅凭这一现象认定某家供应商的零件存在制造缺陷。
苹果方面此前已经承认，少量 iPhone Duo 存在影响内屏的问题，并建议遇到显示故障的用户联系 AppleCare，以便获得更换设备等售后处理。苹果尚未公布具体受影响设备数量，也没有公开确认最终故障原因。
截至10月26日，AppleInsider 通过其联系的20家苹果零售店 Genius Bar 服务点了解到，已知出现相关内屏故障并退回处理的设备共有4台。这一数字仅来自有限的美国零售店样本，并不代表全球故障总数，也无法据此计算产品的实际故障率。
目前，Fine M-Tec 的声明并不能证明其零部件绝对不存在问题，同样，拆解人员发现的断裂部件也不足以证明供应商应当承担责任。要确定事故原因，仍需进一步检查故障设备、分析铰链的实际运动过程，并核对零部件设计、制造公差及装配情况。

units.text: Unlike other iPhones, iPhone Duo can enter StandBy mode without a charger. You only need to fold the Duo in half or in a tent orientation and you'll see widgets, music, calendar, weather, and more – even when you're away from a power source.
Here's how to set up iPhone Duo StandBy mode without a charger:
Open Settings, tap StandBy, and make sure StandBy is turned on.
On the same screen, tick off the folding positions you want to enable, and make sure the Only While Charging toggle is off.
Now, lock your iPhone Duo, partially fold it like a book or a tent, and set it down on a flat surface.

StandBy will start automatically in either supported position. When the display lights up, tap the current face, then swipe left or right to change it to a different style and content mode. Some faces also support swiping up and down to change content.
If you find StandBy to be a power drain, simply turn on Only While Charging to ensure the mode is restricted to charging sessions in future.

units.text: iOS 27.2 is here, and it introduces a new feature for age verification using a selfie. Here are the details.
Apple offers new, privacy-focused way to verify your age in iOS 27.2

An increasing number of territories around the world now require iPhone age verification in certain scenarios, such as when creating an Apple Account, updating your software, downloading apps, or changing select settings.
Per Apple, these requirements may apply to users in Australia, Brazil, Singapore, South Korea, the UK, and also the United States (Texas).
While iOS already offered other methods of age verification, such as using a credit card or scanning your ID, iOS 27.2 adds a new option: taking a selfie.
Per a new support document, Apple says:

In some states, countries, or regions, you might be asked to confirm that you’re an adult before you can take certain actions on your Apple Account. One way to confirm that you’re an adult is to take a selfie. An age-estimation model will then evaluate the images of your face.
The selfie option isn’t available in all regions, but if you’re asked to confirm you’re an adult, you might see the option to use a selfie.
Here’s how it works per Apple’s instructions:
Choose the option to take a selfie, then tap Get Started.
Hold your device in front of you and center your face in the frame.
Capture all four angles of your face by moving your head slowly right, left, up, and down. Follow the onscreen guidance to complete confirmation. It might take a moment to estimate your age.

Apple says your privacy is protected by its age-estimation models running both on-device and on Private Cloud Compute. The selfie “isn’t accessible to anyone, not even Apple.” And after your age has been confirmed, the selfie is deleted immediately and “isn’t retained in any form.”
To learn more about Apple’s new age verification feature in iOS 27.2, read the full support document here.
Have you ever had to perform age verification on your iPhone? How did the process go? Let us know in the comments.

evidence.title: iPhone Duo: Split the Keyboard in Landscape Orientation

units.text: When you're using iPhone Duo unfolded in landscape orientation, you can split the onscreen keyboard into two halves in order to bring the keys closer to your thumbs. It's a longtime iPad option that has now come over to the Duo as an exclusive feature among iPhones.
How to Split the Keyboard on iPhone Duo
It's easy when you know how. Just follow these steps in landscape:
Open an app that accepts text input, then tap a text field to bring up the keyboard.
Tap the More button (...) at the top-left of the keyboard, then tap Split.
To rejoin the two halves, simply tap More again, then tap Full.

Note that the option only appears when iPhone Duo is open and in landscape mode. You won't see it when the device is closed, but what you can do instead is shift the keyboard toward one side of the screen for easier one-handed typing. To do so, long press the globe or emoji key, then tap the left or right layout.

Ironically, one of the big things Apple will be touting for the OLED XDR touch MacBook Pro on Wednesday (ever so slightly thinner case, thinner bezels, noticeably lighter) is its revamped hinge that is more stable so touching the screen doesn't make it rock during usage.

Slightly thinner case
Thinner bezels
Noticeably lighter
Revamped hinge
The new MacBook Pro being thinner and lighter has been reported before. But the thinner bezels and a revamped hinge are new details.

evidence.title: Report: iPhone 18 Pro sales down 4% in the US, but China drives 3.1% global growth

units.text: Counterpoint Research’s latest report offers a look at global iPhone 18 Pro sales during the first three weeks of availability. Here are the details.
Report counters soft demand rumors

In a report released today, Counterpoint Research says iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max sales in the US fell 4% during their first three weeks of availability compared to the first three weeks of iPhone 17 Pro series sales last year.
The report noted that Japan saw a whopping 27% drop in sales, with demand weakening “as exchange rates amplified the price increases.”
China, on the other hand, saw a 29% increase in sales, while other markets collectively recorded a more modest 3.1% increase.
The report doesn’t break down what that means in units, or millions of units, but it does offer some context on what drove these regional differences.
Here’s Counterpoint:

A regional breakdown shows that the global 3.1% growth was concentrated in specific markets. China posted the strongest growth, with sales rising 29% YoY. This was driven by better early supply compared with last year and by price increases on competing flagship models from Chinese Android OEMs. Excluding China’s contribution, the global sales growth rate would have been far weaker. The US and Japan experienced a YoY decline, affected by higher prices compared with their predecessors. In the US, consumers largely do not perceive meaningful improvements over the previous models in either features or design, while in Japan, demand has contracted as exchange rates amplified the price increases.

Today’s report also includes another interesting tidbit: According to Counterpoint, the iPhone 18 Pro Max accounted for a slightly smaller share of Pro-series sales compared to last year’s iPhone 17 Pro series, which the firm attributed to higher prices and stronger demand for the smaller Pro model in emerging markets:

The iPhone 18 Pro Max accounted for 56% of sales within the iPhone 18 Pro series, a slight decrease from 57% last year. This can be attributed to the higher prices compared with last year, as well as the fact that the sales growth in emerging markets such as India and Southeast Asia skewed more toward the Pro models.

As to how, or whether, the iPhone Duo had any effect on these shifting numbers, the report didn’t address that directly, since the device launched after the three-week period covered by the data. However, Counterpoint Associate Director Sujeong Lim raised the possibility that it could affect Pro Max sales going forward:

“Whether China’s outperformance reflects durable demand or front-loaded buying will become clearer in the coming weeks. The recovery of US and Japanese volumes, and whether the iPhone Duo launching in Week 43 will generate incremental demand rather than cannibalising Pro Max, are the two most consequential near-term variables.”
To check out Counterpoint‘s full report, follow this link.

evidence.title: Hinge, dual-layer OLED expectations continue ahead of new MacBook Pro launch

units.text: Hours ahead of Apple's expected touch-enabled MacBook Pro launch, a leaker backs up rumors about price rises and changes to the hinge.

Apple is holding a "Pro and Tell" press event on Wednesday, with it capping off a week of updates. That event is expected to include not only the iPad mini, iMac, and M6 MacBook Pro for members of the media to try out, but also an OLED MacBook Pro.

The evening before the event, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital decided to post about the upcoming launch and what to expect. Bumping up an earlier post saying it would be an OLED display with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, they added a bit more detail about the major changes.
The touchscreen will use a dual-layer OLED display, they claim. This is a display tech that Apple has used before in the iPad Pro for a brighter and more power-efficient panel.

Including such a panel in the MacBook Pro seems like a natural progression for the tech. It's also something that will significantly increase the price of the inbound model, in the leaker's estimation.
Hinge changes

Fixed Focus Digital also insists that Apple is improving the hinge design of the new MacBook Pro. This is apparently in line with the development of hinges for the iPhone Duo's second- and third-generation models.
A change of hinge does make sense, as the display will have to cope with being tapped by the user in daily use.

However, linking it to the hinges of future iPhone Duo versions is a strange claim. The iPhone Duo's hinge is made specifically with the flexible display in mind, which the MacBook Pro wouldn't have barring a major overhaul of the product line.
A call for attention
While the Fixed Focus Digital post is framed to make the leaker seem as authoritative as possible, it doesn't quite manage to achieve that effect.

The post includes elements that are just an educated guess away for anyone who has followed the OLED MacBook Pro rumors. There's very little new in the post, and it feels like a "me too" post made after the information was already out there

By contrast, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman posted on Tuesday night with a more detailed assessment of the next MacBook Pro launch. He specified prices, such as the $400 price increase over the non-OLED version for the 14-inch M5 Pro model.

Gurman also discussed the OLED XDR displays, including the use of a Dynamic Island, slimmer bodies, and a lighter overall weight. There was even a brief mention of a redesigned hinge so that the screen stays put while users touch it.
In comparison, the Fixed Focus Digital post serves as a reminder to the account's followers that they are active in the rumor scene.

evidence.raw_lead: One of the advantages of the iPhone Duo's folding design is that you aren't limited to using the front camera when taking self-portraits. It may sound counterintuitive, but by unfolding the device, you can flip it around and take selfies with the higher-quality 48MP rear Fusion cameras instead.
evidence.title: iPhone Duo: Take Selfies With Rear Cameras for Higher Quality Shots

units.text: One of the advantages of the iPhone Duo's folding design is that you aren't limited to using the front camera when taking self-portraits. It may sound counterintuitive, but by unfolding the device, you can flip it around and take selfies with the higher-quality 48MP rear Fusion cameras instead.

The Duo's outer display is what makes this use case practical, since once the rear cameras are pointing at you, it shows a live preview along with the camera controls – so you can frame the shot before you take it. Keep reading to learn how it's done.
How to Take Selfies With the Rear Cameras on iPhone Duo
Unfold your iPhone Duo and open the Camera app.
Turn the phone around so that the rear cameras are pointing toward you.
Drag the Show Camera slider on the outer display to bring the Camera app onto that screen.
Frame your shot on the outer display, then tap the shutter button, or press either volume button or Camera Control.

Note that the rear-camera selfie option only works when your iPhone Duo is open. If you want the person you're photographing to see themselves instead, that's a different feature called Duo Preview – see our separate how-to for the details.

One of the advantages of the iPhone Duo's folding design is that you aren't limited to using the front camera when taking self-portraits. It may sound counterintuitive, but by unfolding the device, you can flip it around and take selfies with the higher-quality 48MP rear Fusion cameras instead.
Unfold your iPhone Duo and open the Camera app.
Turn the phone around so that the rear cameras are pointing toward you.
Drag the Show Camera slider on the outer display to bring the Camera app onto that screen.
Frame your shot on the outer display, then tap the shutter button, or press either volume button or Camera Control.

units.text: 彭博社记者马克·古尔曼在苹果Pro and Tell活动前夕释出最后爆料，苹果首款搭载OLED触摸屏的MacBook Pro将于明日正式登场。这款被寄予厚望的旗舰机型不仅引入了触控交互，起售价更是刷新了纪录，14英寸版本预计从2899美元（约合人民币20658元）起售。
先说定价，新款触摸屏版MacBook Pro将作为产品线中的超高端型号，与现有的非触摸屏版本并行销售。这意味着如果你追求最新的硬件设计，必须支付极高的溢价。
以16英寸机型为例，其起售价预计至少为3399美元（约合人民币24221元），相比四个月前M5 Pro机型的起步价，涨幅高达700美元（约合人民币4988元）。
外观与性能方面，这款新机第一次用上带灵动岛的OLED触控屏，色彩和对比度会提升一大截，搭载M5 Pro、M5 Max芯片。
整个机身则做得更薄更轻，屏幕边框也收窄了，另外苹果还重新调校了转轴阻尼，避免用户点屏幕的时候机身晃来晃去
散热方面也进行了大刀阔斧的改革，新的散热模组重构了气流路径，空气直接通过转轴部位进行交换，这在提升散热效率的同时，也帮助机身实现了进一步减重。
这种设计不仅是为了应付触控操作带来的额外功耗，也是为了维持OLED面板在长时间高亮度下的寿命。
除此之外，古尔曼还曝光了苹果决定给Mac加上触屏的背后故事：据他的消息源透露，库克大约在四年前就拍板立项触屏MacBook Pro，很大一部分原因是用户对这项功能的呼声一直很高。
知情人士表示：“库克当时认为，这件事我们该做了。”

evidence.title: New M6 Macs buck Apple’s second wave of price hikes

units.text: In addition to the spec bumps, today’s M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro announcements came with an extra piece of good news: prices remained unchanged from the previous generations, unlike several other recent Apple product launches that brought another round of increases. Here are the details.
Prices unchanged, for a change
Earlier today, Apple announced two new M6-powered Macs, which start at the same prices as their predecessors.

And while both models benefit from the faster M6 chip, iMac buyers are also getting more CPU and GPU cores for the same price, as the base model now comes with a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, up from the 8-core CPU and 8-core GPU in the previous generation’s M4 chip.

As 9to5Mac readers probably remember, Apple raised prices across much of its product lineup in June, including the iMac, which went from $1,299 to $1,499, and the 14-inch MacBook Pro, which went from $1,699 to $1,999.
At the time, the company also hiked prices for the HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K, and iPad mini, all of which saw new versions announced recently with yet another price bump.

The HomePod mini, which went from $99 to $129 in June, now costs $149 with the second-generation model. The Apple TV 4K, which previously started at $129, jumped to $199 in June, while the new generation starts at $299 (albeit with twice the storage). And the iPad mini, which went from $499 to $599 in June, now starts at $699 with the OLED model announced earlier this week.

And while iPhone prices were left untouched during the June increases, that changed in September with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which now start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively, up $100 from their predecessors.
Apple also raised prices by $100 for the older iPhone models still in its lineup, including the iPhone 17, iPhone Air, and iPhone 17e.
With that in mind, although the new M6-powered Macs are far from cheap, it’s still good news that they didn’t come with another price hike on top of the June increases.

Things are looking way less promising for those waiting for tomorrow’s expected OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models, however, with Bloomberg reporting that Apple has discussed a $2,899 starting price for the 14-inch model. If Apple applies the same rumored $400 premium to the current 16-inch model, which starts at $2,999, the new version could cost $3,399 or more.

That, in turn, makes Apple’s decision to keep prices unchanged for today’s M6-powered Macs all the more welcome, especially for buyers who were already dreading the possibility of having to shell out even more after waiting for the new models. Whether that will hold remains to be seen.
What’s your take on Apple’s pricing strategy for the M6 Macs announced earlier today? Let us know in the comments.

evidence.title: iPhone 18 Pro sales beat iPhone 17 Pro figures, but only because of China

units.text: Contrary to complaints from stock analysts about poor iPhone 18 Pro sales, new supply chain research claims that the demand for the iPhone 18 Pro has been high in China, making up for some weakness elsewhere.

It was already clear that the iPhone 18 Pro had sold well as it appears to have been key to Apple reaching a $5 trillion market valuation. But in a note sent to AppleInsider, Counterpoint Research says that demand has been more patchy and region-specific than with the iPhone 17 Pro.

Sales of the iPhone 18 Pro models in China over the first three weeks after release were up 29% year over year. That was helped, though, by how Apple had more stocks of the new model than they had of the iPhone 17 Pro at launch.
Also, demand for Android smartphones from local Chinese firms fell because of price increases.
This clearly made the iPhone more appealing in China. But the demand in that country was such that the iPhone 18 Pro's overall global sales were up 3.1% compared to the iPhone 17 Pro.

These figures are all for the initial demand of the iPhone models and Counterpoint's associate director Sujeong Lim cautions that "Whether China's outperformance reflects durable demand or front-loaded buying will become clearer in the coming weeks."
Lim also says that the research firm is looking to see whether the iPhone Duo's later launch than the other models will cannibalize sales, or generate fresh, incremental demand.
Taking China out of the equation

Counterpoint Research says that in the US, sales were down 4% year over year, and speculates that this is because buyers didn't find sufficient improvements to warrant upgrading for. However, 4% is more likely to be the number of US buyers who elected to wait for the iPhone Duo instead of buying the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max.

Then there was also a dramatic downturn in Japan as sales there were 27% down from the iPhone 17 Pro's figures. However, that was reportedly due in part to increased iPhone prices being exacerbated by higher exchange rates.
As ever, the iPhone 18 Pro Max accounted for the majority of sales across every territory. Although for the 2026 iPhones, 56% were the Max edition, compared to 57% in 2025.
This time Apple split its launch so that it only released the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the new iPhone Duo. The usual base iPhone 18 model will now be launched sometime early in 2027.

One analyst believes this split means Apple has lost sales that it won't get back, which doesn't make sense to us, given the seasonality of the iPhone market. Others have reported that Apple has cut iPhone 18 Pro orders, although JP Morgan analysts have dismissed those claims.

units.text: Apple is expected to announce its touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro on October 27. On October 26, I still find it impossible to really grasp who this machine is for and if anyone is really crying out for what seems to be a MacBook More-Pro.

There have long been rumors of Apple's plans to release a new laptop that will sit above the current 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros in its lineup. It may or may not be called the MacBook Ultra, although it seems unlikely at this point.

The name is just one question mark that continues to loom large over what should otherwise be an exciting new laptop. There's talk of an OLED display, a first for Apple's Mac lineup, as well as Apple's almost range-topping M5 Pro and M5 Max silicon.

We've also heard claims of a (slightly) new industrial design, with Apple ditching the familiar notch and replacing it with an iPhone-like Dynamic Island. A lighter, possibly even thinner construction has also been rumored.
And then, there's the main point that this laptop rumor has hung its hat on for what feels like forever. The new not-MacBook-Ultra-but-also-maybe is expected to be the first Mac with a touchscreen.
But as the 2007 meme also ponders, "y tho?"
A break from tradition

Apple, famously, once argued that touchscreen laptops were a big no-no. None other than Craig Federighi, Apple's head of software engineering, argued as much at a time when every other company was falling over themselves to bring touch to their computers.

"We really feel that the ergonomics of using a Mac are that your hands are rested on a surface, and that lifting your arm up to poke a screen is a pretty fatiguing thing to do," Federighi said when discussing the possibility of bringing touch to the Mac in June 2018. "I don't think we've looked at any of the other guys to date and said, how fast can we get there?"
He went further, arguing that Windows touchscreen laptops were nothing more than "experiments." But just two years later, things were changing.
The OLED MacBook Pro may be the end of the notch
A patent published in 2020 highlighted Apple's work to bring touch to the Mac. At the time, it was suggested that users could touch their laptop display to interact with an iPhone or similar device.
Fast-forward to October 2026, and it seems Apple is finally ready to launch a touchscreen MacBook Pro.
But again, I'm left wondering why.

More importantly, I'm wondering who such a feature is really for, and how it will actually work. Apple's macOS is designed with cursor input in mind, with small targets like window controls that just aren't built to be tapped with meaty fingers.
Apple already makes software that's built with a touch-first mindset. It's called iPadOS, and you can get it right now on an array of computers called iPads.
You can even try it out a bit with Sidecar. It's pretty nasty business, though, unless you're using an Apple Pencil.

I'd argue that Apple was right the first time out when it said that poking a laptop display doesn't sound like a fun way to use a desktop or laptop computer. I've yet to see a use case that makes the hassle, or the fingerprints, worth it.
There's little else here

The problem is, without the touch element, this impending MacBook Pro announcement makes even less sense. If it's going to use the same chips as the current model, and we agree that touching it is lunacy, there's little else going for it.
The move to an OLED display will be the headline-grabber, sure. OLED promises deep contrast and vibrant colors plus lightning-fast response times.
But anyone who has used one of Apple's mini-LED laptops will tell you that they already boast stunning displays. Almost too bright in some instances, with gorgeous colors and strong contrast figures.
Nobody accused Apple's Liquid Display XDR of lacking brightness or anything else
If the move to OLED brings the end of the notch, then so be it. But I don't foresee many MacBook Pro buyers ditching their current laptop just to get a Dynamic Island.
And if the new model does use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, it won't be any faster than its predecessor, either. Yet it'll presumably command a higher price.

Which again raises the question, "y tho?" I could get behind the idea of an OLED MacBook Pro if it were replacing the current models wholesale, but it doesn't appear to be the case. Apple announced a new non-OLED 14-inch MacBook Pro this very day, after all.

The way I see it, there are only two ways that the fabled OLED MacBook Pro makes sense. Either it has some knockout feature that hasn't leaked yet, or Apple has an especially compelling story for the features that have.
In lieu of either, for now at least, I'm left wondering just what market a new OLED MacBook Pro really serves.

evidence.title: Apple introduces the new 14‑inch MacBook Pro with M6

units.text: CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive.1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power.2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance.3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy.4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere.3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6. “The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.” M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive. The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5.2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5.3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling.2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 helps motion designers model 3D objects, design product visualizations, and render animations with ease.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables:3
Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Film editors and content creators can quickly and efficiently composite visual effects and add cinematic motion graphics in popular video editing tools on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6.
Photographers and designers can make complex AI-powered image adjustments in real time using apps like Pixelmator Pro on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6.
Developers can build and test their apps with blazing-fast compile times in Xcode on the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6.

There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:

Phenomenal battery life: In addition to the huge leap in performance, battery life gets up to 14 additional hours for Intel-based upgraders and up to four more hours for users coming from M1, delivering up to 24 hours overall, so users can get more done on a single charge. Users coming from Intel-based and M1 systems will also get 16GB of starting unified memory, an additional Thunderbolt port, and the space black finish with an anodization seal for fewer fingerprints.

A brilliant pro display: The stunning Liquid Retina XDR display delivers up to 1600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio, bringing HDR photos and videos to life with deep blacks, brilliant highlights, and vibrant colors. And for users working in bright or challenging lighting conditions, a nano-texture display option dramatically reduces reflections and glare.

Powerful connectivity: Now with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro delivers fast wireless performance and low latency, along with support for up to two external displays. Its versatile array of ports — including the HDMI, MagSafe 3, and three Thunderbolt 4 ports; an SDXC card slot; and a headphone jack — makes it easy to connect high-speed peripherals, transfer photos, or expand a workspace.

Advanced camera, mics, and speakers: A 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View helps keep users perfectly framed on video calls, while a studio-quality three-mic array and amazing six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio deliver an immersive audio experience.

Fast charging: MacBook Pro with M6 supports fast charging, reaching up to 50 percent charge in just 30 minutes when paired with a compatible higher-wattage USB-C power adapter, such as the 96W Power Adapter.3
A laptop that’s built to last: With an enclosure made from 100 percent recycled aluminum, MacBook Pro is exceptionally durable and can stand up to everyday use for years to come.

Better together with iPhone: When used together with Continuity, iPhone and Mac are even more powerful — letting users move seamlessly across devices to share files and photos, hand off tasks, and even control their iPhone from their 14-inch MacBook Pro.5 Users switching to Mac for the first time can use iPhone to conveniently and securely transfer settings, files, photos, passwords, and more.

The brilliant Liquid Retina XDR display delivers up to 1600 nits of peak HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio. HDR photos and videos look more true to life with deep blacks, brilliant highlights, and vibrant colors.
With the new 14-inch MacBook Pro, users can connect high-speed peripherals, transfer photos, work with multiple external displays, and more with its wide array of ports.

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall,6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based7 and designed to be recycled. Pricing and Availability

Customers can pre-order the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starting tomorrow, October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 35 countries and regions, including the U.S. It will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Friday, November 6.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 (U.S.) and $1,899 (U.S.) with education savings. Additional technical specifications and configure-to-order options are available at apple.com/macbook-pro.

With Apple Upgrade, eligible customers in the U.S. can lease a new Mac with low monthly payments and easily upgrade at the end of their lease.8 Lease the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 with Apple Upgrade from $38.99 (U.S.) per month, excluding taxes and any trade-in credit, for 36 months.^

With Apple Trade In, customers can trade in their current computer and get credit toward a new Mac. Customers can visit apple.com/shop/trade-in to see what their device is worth. With year-round education pricing — available to current and newly accepted college students and educators — customers can save on MacBook Pro, along with a wide range of products and services through the Apple Store online and in stores. Visit the Apple Education Store for details. Customers in the U.S. who shop at Apple using Apple Card9 can pay monthly at 0 percent APR when they choose to check out with Apple Card Monthly Installments,10 and they’ll get 3 percent Daily Cash back — all up front. More information — including details on eligibility, exclusions, and Apple Card terms — is available at apple.com/apple-card/monthly-installments.

AppleCare delivers exceptional service and support, with flexible options for Apple users. Customers can choose AppleCare+ to cover their new Mac or, in available markets, AppleCare One to protect multiple products in one simple plan. Both plans include coverage for accidents like drops and spills, theft and loss protection on eligible products, battery replacement service, and priority support from Apple Experts. In the U.S., customers can also choose AppleCare One Family, which extends that same coverage to every eligible device across an Apple Family Sharing group for one fixed monthly price. For more information, visit apple.com/applecare.

Every customer who buys directly from Apple gets access to Personal Setup. In these guided one-on-one online sessions, a Specialist can walk them through setup or focus on features that will help them make the most of their new device. Customers can also learn more about getting started and going further with their new device with a Today at Apple session at their nearest Apple Store.

evidence.title: Apple knows the iPad mini market, but internet unimpressed by 60Hz

units.text: Apple yesterday officially launched what it describes as “the biggest update ever” to the iPad mini, featuring an OLED screen and a thinner, lighter design.
However, while there are a significant number of upgrades, internet commentators were very focused on the one thing Apple didn’t upgrade: that 60Hz display …
Apple highlighted the new features.

A stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support.

Commenters, however, were quick to point to the fact that the refresh rate wasn’t mentioned, with the obvious conclusion that it remains 60Hz instead of being updated to a ProMotion variable refresh rate of 1 to 120Hz.
“700 bucks and no 120hz display?”
“I was someone interested in adding a mini but at 60hz, 128gb, no Face ID I can’t justify the already inflated price tag.”
“60Hz right? in 2026 right? Hell no.”
“60Hz? Next…”
“60Hz in 2026. Apple should be ashamed.”
View all comments

I could include many more quotes, but you get the idea. It’s certainly a surprising omission in a 2026 device, especially when our sister site 9to5Google noted that the closest Android competitor has a 185Hz refresh rate.

The biggest point in Redmagic’s favor is in that display, too. Where Apple is still refusing to give the iPad Mini a 120Hz refresh rate with this latest model – utterly insane in the year two thousand and twenty-six, if I do say so myself – Astra 2 has a 185Hz refresh rate. I’ve not found that inherently better than a standard 120Hz panel, but it’s way better than the 60Hz panel Apple’s latest will still be using.

Now I fully acknowledge that Apple knows the iPad mini market better than any of us do. I’m also aware that it has historically been primarily a business device, used for applications ranging from restaurant waitstaff relaying orders to the kitchen through mobile payment terminals to warehouse inventory systems. None of these types of applications would remotely benefit from a display with a faster refresh rate.

Additionally, when it comes to consumers, I’m sure it’s true that not everyone appreciates the benefits of 120Hz. Some of those in our comments claimed they couldn’t tell the difference, while others said it was only really relevant to gaming. Adding that category of individual purchasers to the majority business market, and Apple has undoubtedly correctly concluded that the majority of its customers simply don’t care about this feature.

However … Those who do care about it, care about it rather a lot. I don’t know what the unit cost difference would be, but since 120Hz is now standard on a great many cheaper devices, I can’t imagine it’s a substantial one. I can’t help feeling that this is a case where Apple simply should have done the right thing, even if only a minority of buyers would appreciate it.

’Boost mode’

Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip. The announcement came alongside new, M6-powered iMacs, and on the eve of the expected announcement of its first OLED MacBook Pro models with touchscreen support.
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999, with pre-orders opening tomorrow, October 28, and availability beginning November 6.
It features a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU that’s up to 30% faster than the M5, a dual 16-core Neural Engine, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and support for fast charging. You can learn more about it here.

Following the announcement, Apple also released the 14-inch MacBook Pro ad on its YouTube channel. The ad touts its faster graphics, faster AI performance, and battery life, and you can watch it below:

Apple also published a 1-minute promo video that dives deeper into the new features and tech specs, including its Liquid Retina XDR display, connectivity specs, and how it fits into the broader Apple Silicon family. Watch it below:

Today’s announcements came just one day after Apple unveiled the new OLED iPad mini, which features a thinner and lighter design, a larger 8.5-inch display, the A20 Pro chip, improved audio, and IP67 water and dust resistance. It starts at $699, with pre-orders opening tomorrow and availability beginning November 6.
To learn more about the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6, follow this link.

units.text: 苹果最新一代高端手机 iPhone 18 Pro 系列上市后的初期销售表现呈现明显的区域分化。市场研究机构 Counterpoint Research 的供应链调查显示，iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max上市前三周的全球销量同比增长3.1%，但这一增长很大程度上依赖中国市场的强劲表现。如果剔除中国市场，苹果新一代Pro系列的整体销售增长将明显减弱。
Counterpoint Research的数据显示，iPhone 18 Pro系列在中国上市前三周的销量同比增长29%，是此次全球销售增长的主要推动力。相比之下，美国市场销量同比下降4%，日本市场则大幅下降27%。印度市场的表现相对积极，但研究机构并未公布该市场的具体增长比例。
这一结果说明，苹果新一代高端手机并未在所有主要市场同步获得增长，而是呈现出中国市场强劲、部分成熟市场疲软的局面。尽管全球销量仍高于上一代产品，但仅凭3.1%的整体增幅，还不足以证明新机在全球范围内获得了广泛而均衡的需求。
中国市场的强劲表现，与两个因素有关。首先，苹果今年新机上市初期的备货情况好于上一代产品，这意味着更多消费者能够在首发阶段直接购买

units.text: Opening Control Center on iPhone normally means swiping down from the top-right corner of the screen, but the iPhone Duo features a second, easier way to invoke the controls. Keep reading to learn how it's done.
Tap to Open Control Center on iPhone Duo
With your iPhone Duo unlocked, tap the circular status bar below the clock (the combined Wi-Fi, cellular and battery indicator).
When Control Center opens, you'll also see the status bar expand into its individual Wi-Fi, cellular and battery parts.

The shortcut saves you stretching your finger to the top-right corner, making Control Center easier to reach one-handed. Also, when a Live Activity is running, the status bar moves even further down the screen, so it comes within even easier reach.

evidence.title: Judge grants yet more of Apple's requests for OpenAI information

units.text: As the case inches closer to trial, OpenAI has been ordered to surrender more details to Apple about its employees' use of devices and tools, and its recruitment practices.

Apple has been pressing for early discovery in its lawsuit against OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft, arguing that delays materially hurt it. Judge Edward Davila has previously tended to side with Apple, but denied it certain information because he said the requests were too broad.

Now Apple has narrowed the scope of its requests, specifically changing it from covering all ex-Apple employees to being specifically those hired by OpenAI. On that basis, Judge Davila has granted more of the requests and so ordered OpenAI to provide Apple with details of:
Ex-Apple Employee Chang Liu's and Tang Tan's devices used to store confidential Apple information
Their accounts and messaging apps containing the same
Their use of AI tools for both personal and OpenAI work
Any confidential Apple information that may have been destroyed
OpenAI is also ordered to provide testimonies about Apple information specifically used in battery technologies and metal finishings.
The ChatGPT maker must also detail how it did or did not try to prevent the use of confidential information. And it is required to detail recruitment interviews it had with Apple employees.
Apple didn't get everything - yet

However, Judge Davila denied Apple's requests for many specific details such as OpenAI's own investigations into this issue. Apple has not been granted access to certain other details about OpenAI devices and accounts used by the ex-Apple employees either.
That may not change, but two further requests the judge denied are likely to. Judge Davila turned down Apple's requests for certain testimonies, but only because they were too broad.

Specifically, Judge Davila ruled that certain such requests were "more appropriately addressed through ordinary merits discovery, which neither Party appears to dispute should be conducted efficiently." So once the trial proper gets underway, Apple may be able to get these particular requests granted.

Few lawsuits are conducted speedily, but this one has had more visible back and forth between Apple, OpenAI, and the judge because of Apple's urging for emergency discovery. OpenAI appears to have abandoned its claims of not having used confidential information, but it has also attempted to delay certain parts of the proceedings for as long as possible.

In theory, that would have allowed OpenAI more time to use the information and to produce its expected AI hardware device. Most recently, OpenAI voluntarily promised not to use such information, however.
That may have been the company just trying to get ahead of an inevitable court order. But now it has 14 days to comply with the latest ruling.

units.text: iOS 27.2 and its corresponding updates for the HomePod lineup bring several key new features to Apple’s smart speakers. The most exciting update? The ability to finally use your HomePod as the default sound output for your Mac. This means that the 2nd-generation HomePod and HomePod mini 2 can now function as low-latency wireless speakers for your Mac!

Watch our hands-on video for an in-depth look at how the new wireless speaker functionality works, along with other new features like Sound Glow, Lock Controls, and home theater surround sound support. Be sure to subscribe to our YouTube channel for more in-depth videos.
HomePod as speakers for Mac

It’s long been possible to use a HomePod as a wireless speaker for the Mac, but doing so came with at least one big caveat: wireless latency. While it’s generally fine for movie playback, the latency is immediately noticeable when playing anything in real time. For example, playing instruments in Logic Pro, audio and FaceTime calls, etc. For these particular applications, HomePods have, up until now, been less than ideal speakers for the Mac.
Video walkthrough
Subscribe to 9to5Mac on YouTube for more videos

Apple has addressed this issue in the 27.2 update, significantly reducing latency when using a HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) as a wireless speaker for Mac desktops and laptops that support Wi-Fi 6E. This, unfortunately, excludes some early Apple Silicon machines, such as those powered by the M1 family of chips, but it’s good to see this feature made available.
HomePod 2nd Generation set as the Default System Output Device in System Profiler

For the HomePod mini 2, Apple included a different Wi-Fi/Bluetooth architecture based on PCIe and revised audio routing to prioritize low-latency applications. It’s also worth noting that Apple’s Wi-Fi 6E requirement applies to the Mac hardware itself and doesn’t imply that a user needs a 6E-enabled router.
HomePod 1 vs HomePod 2 latency test with Logic Pro

From that, we can gather that the update will allow the HomePod to work similarly to how it currently works with an Apple TV, when set as the default audio source. In other words, instead of relying on traditional AirPlay, it creates an ad hoc point-to-point connection between the Mac and the HomePod for minimal latency. This will make a HomePod a viable speaker-output destination for real-time audio applications.
Notice that the Play sound effects through setting now allows for AirPlay

Apple is so confident of the low-latency connection that it defaults to playing sound effects via AirPlay when a compatible HomePod is selected as the output destination. Obviously, sound effects are the sort of thing that relies on low latency, since their sound has to correspond to what is happening in the environment at that exact time; otherwise, it would be disorienting. If I select my HomePod mini (1st generation), that option is not even available.
The Play sound effects through setting doesn’t allow for AirPlay on older HomePod hardware

Needless to say, this update instantly has me reconsidering my speaker needs for my Mac desktop setup. I recently got rid of my Yamaha HS3s because I’m looking for something with a little more umph. A pair of full-sized 2nd-generation HomePods in a stereo pair would definitely fit the bill, and look much better to boot.
Lock Controls

Have you ever accidentally brushed the touch sensor on the top cap of the HomePod, activating it to play music? Do you have pets who surreptitiously activate your HomePod while you’re not in the room? If so, then the new Lock Controls switch in 27.2 will help.

When Lock Controls is enabled, the touch surface on top of the HomePod is locked, meaning touch, touch-and-hold, and volume adjustments are disabled. You’ll easily recognize when Lock Controls is enabled by the bright red “no” animation that appears.
Even the first-gen HomePod gets some love

Lock Controls will prevent a HomePod from playing audio or taking action when the device’s top cap is touched. However, intercom, alarms, timers, Check in, and FaceTime calls will continue to respond to touch.

Of all the new features in the 27.2 software update, Lock Controls is the only one that appears on all HomePod models, regardless of generation. That means that, yes, even the original OG HomePod lands support for the handy new addition!
Sound Glow

My favorite new feature in the 27.2 update is Sound Glow. This is the feature that displays ambient light that corresponds to the colors and rhythm of the album artwork for the music or podcasts being played.

Sound Glow takes full advantage of the LED Matrix displays beneath the HomePod top cap. The big HomePod features an array of 37 RGB LEDs, while the smaller HomePod mini features an array of 19 RGB LEDs. As a side note, the original HomePod features 19 LEDs across a smaller surface area than the updated version.

To enable Sound Glow, you must update your iOS device and your HomePod to 27.2. Once updated, open the Home app and venture into the settings for the HomePod you wish to adjust. There, you’ll find a Sound Glow switch you can enable.

Apple notes that you’ll also be able to toggle Sound Glow with your voice, but it will require an Apple Intelligence‑enabled iPhone running the latest software. This could be enabled once Apple enables Siri AI on the HomePod mini 2, and perhaps the 2nd-generation HomePod, but this remains to be seen.
Home theater surround sound

If you plan to purchase an Apple TV 4K (fourth-generation), you’re likely interested in the new home theater surround sound option available with the HomePod mini 2 or the 2nd-generation full-sized HomePod. This feature lets you use four HomePods, two identical matching stereo pairs in front and rear, for a surround sound setup.

I haven’t been able to personally test this yet, because I don’t yet have the newest Apple TV 4K, but I can bet it will sound fantastic, especially when four full-sized Dolby Atmos-enabled HomePods are involved. That being said, this is an expensive proposition.
Here are the pricing details for those looking to set up a four-speaker home theater surround sound option:
Apple TV 4K ($299) + Four HomePod 2 ($349×4) = $1695
Apple TV 4K ($299) + Two HomePod 2 ($349×2) + two HomePod mini 2 ($149×2) = $1295
Apple TV 4K ($299) + Four HomePod mini 2 ($149×4) = $895

By way of comparison, Sonos’ Dolby Atmos-enabled four-speaker Immersive Set with Beam Ultra bundle can be had for less than $1600 and comes with a dedicated subwoofer. I’m not a home audio expert or an audiophile, so I can’t say which one is better, but it’s interesting that both it and the highest-tier HomePod surround setup are so similar in price.

When managing your HomePod speakers via the tvOS interface on the Apple TV 4K, you’ll see new options for Surround Sound and Whole Room Audio under the Home Theater section. The surround sound option is self-explanatory and ideal for movies and television shows, but the Whole Room Audio option is better suited to listening to music, as it provides left- and right-channel placement no matter which direction you face.
9to5Mac’s Take

iOS 27.2 provides noteworthy updates to all HomePod models, including the original HomePod, which now includes the new Lock Controls capability. But the real fun starts with the HomePod mini, with its Sound Glow support, and the HomePod mini 2 and HomePod 2nd-generation, with their support for working as the default speaker for Wi-Fi 6E-enabled Mac hardware. I think a pair of HomePod mini 2’s would look great sitting next to Apple’s just-released M6 iMac.

What do you think? Are you planning to get any of Apple’s new Home-focused hardware, or are you looking to take advantage of the new 27.2 features on hardware you already own? Sound off in the comments with your thoughts on the matter.

units.text: 苹果终于对「摇一摇」广告动手了！
今天凌晨，苹果正式推送了 iOS 27.2 系统更新。
这次更新里藏着一个让所有国内 iPhone 用户喜大普奔的「史诗级」功能——限制动作数据（Restrict Motion Data）。
不夸张地说，对于苦开屏广告久矣的国内 iPhone 用户而言，这可能是近三年最值得连夜升级的一次小版本更新。这回，苹果也算是亲自下场向「摇一摇」跳转广告宣战。
我们在第一时间将手机升级到了 iOS 27.2 正式版，替大家跑了一遍实测，看看它到底能不能彻底治好开屏乱跳。
四步告别「摇一摇」
升级到 iOS 27.2 后，只需四步就能开启这个功能：
进入「设置」—「隐私与安全」，下滑找到「运动与健身」，滑到底部点击新增的「限制动作数据」，再点开右上角的「编辑」，把平时开屏最爱乱跳的 App 一一勾选进列表即可。
它的底层逻辑其实非常简单粗暴：
苹果在系统底层加了一道闸，直接禁止名单里的 App 读取陀螺仪和加速度计数据。一旦某个 App 被关进这个小黑屋，无论开屏画面上的小图标摇得多欢，手机传感器对它来说都是彻底的瞎子。
为了验证这个开关到底是不是「心理安慰」，我们也挑了几个平时开屏广告极其灵敏的重灾区 App 进行了实测。
在未开启之前，仅仅是正常抬手或轻微晃动，开屏画面就会瞬间识别触发，不到半秒就直接跳进了淘宝。
加入「限制动作数据」名单后，部分应用的开屏依然会出现写着「摇动手机或点击了解更多」的广告画面，但无论我们怎么剧烈摇晃手机，整个页面都纹丝不动，直到 5 秒倒计时结束，老老实实地进入了 App 首页——
毕竟这个功能只负责掐断传感器数据，并不屏蔽广告画面本身。
有意思的是，我们在实测中还观察到，另一部分应用在发现读取不到陀螺仪数据后，干脆不再加载「摇一摇」图标，而是直接退回到了传统的静态开屏广告，这或许与各家广告 SDK 的备选策略有关。
唯有百度网盘是个例外。在我们多次测试中，其摇一摇广告仍有极小概率被意外触发。我们猜测，它的广告跳转机制并不完全依赖陀螺仪和加速度计，还可能混入了其他触发逻辑。
另外在实测中我们还发现一个小限制：这个功能不挑手机硬件版本，无论国行还是外版 iPhone 都能用，但必须登录中国大陆区的 Apple ID 才会显示。如果你中途把商店账号切回美区或港区，这个设置入口就会直接消失。
图｜左图为美区账号 右图为国区账号
至于怎么选，爱范儿并不建议大家一股脑把手机里的所有应用全部勾上。因为苹果这次采用的是全局「一刀切」逻辑，一旦拉黑，App 在正常使用过程中也彻底拿不到陀螺仪和加速度计数据。
因此，遇到本身高度依赖传感器的 App 就需要格外谨慎，比如百度地图 / 高德地图（步行导航依赖陀螺仪判断人体朝向）、Keep（体感运动计数）或是《和平精英》（陀螺仪辅助压枪）。
我比较推荐的使用方式是：平时先不用管，哪天打开某个 App 被开屏摇一摇暗算了，再反手把它加进黑名单里。
专钻空子的「鬼才」发明
很多人可能已经记不清，自己是从哪一天开始，每次点开手机 App 都要下意识端平手腕，像端着一碗滚烫的热汤一样如履薄冰。
其实把「摇晃手机」作为互动触发手段并不新鲜。真正让这项交互变味、并演变成中文互联网公敌的转折点，发生在 2021 年。
那一年，移动广告行业迎来了强监管的洗礼：国内工信部掀起了一轮针对 App 开屏弹窗的专项整治，重点打击两件事——「跳过按钮小如蚊子腿」和「全屏文字诱导点击」。
老路被监管堵死，但各家流量平台对开屏广告的转化率考核却一天都没放松。
一边是合规压力，一边是商业焦虑。急于保住变现效率的厂商，很快在手机系统里找到了一个完美的「后门」——运动传感器。
那为什么偏偏是「摇一摇」这个功能？在当时的主流移动操作系统中，相机、麦克风和定位属于需要弹窗授权的「敏感权限」；唯独加速度计和陀螺仪这类基础传感器，被系统视为人畜无害的底层接口，App 启动即可默认静默读取，连个招呼都不用打。
在广告平台眼里，这简直是天降救星——
既然监管不让做全屏点击热区，那就直接读取零门槛的陀螺仪数据。只要检测到手机发生晃动或倾斜，广告 SDK 就默认「用户表达了强烈的互动意愿」，顺理成章地完成跳转。
到了 2021 年双 11 期间，这套能力彻底成了各大广告联盟的标配，几乎所有国民级 App 一夜之间全学会了这一招。
而尝到转化率暴涨甜头的厂商，很快就让这项交互彻底走向了失控：
首先是被调到反人类的触发阈值。尽管后来相关行业协会出台了标准，规定摇一摇触发的加速度不应小于 $15\text{ m/s}^2$、转动角度需大于 $35^\circ$，但在各种流量考核压力下，无数 App 选择了阳奉阴违。地铁进站刹车的惯性、走路时步伐的微弱震动，甚至只是想要「点击跳过广告按钮」的这个动作本身，都会被高敏传感器瞬间捕获。
最让人血压飙升的，是在我们的真实使用场景当中。
当早高峰你正站在地铁闸机口急着调出乘车码，手腕稍微一抖，瞬间唤醒了购物软件，紧接着又弹出一个领红包弹窗；等你顶着身后排队的视线、手忙脚乱地切回原软件，刚才的页面要么得重新加载，要么干脆又刷出了一条新的 5 秒广告。
为什么一个本该服务于人的交互接口，最后会异化成处处给用户使绊子的陷阱？这其实和互联网过去许多令人讨厌的设计如出一辙。
如果从产品设计的视角看，摇一摇广告的泛滥，其实是互联网「暗黑模式」（Dark Patterns）一次极其恶劣的降维进化。
2010 年，英国交互设计师 Harry Brignull 首次提出了「暗黑模式」的概念，用来指代那些并非因为设计师水平差、而是故意利用人类认知盲区和心理惯性，诱导用户做出违背自身意愿、却有利于平台利益的设计。
过去十几年里，我们对这套把戏并不陌生：卸载软件时把「残忍离开」做成灰底小字，把「继续使用」做成高亮大按钮；又比如购买机票时默认勾选在角落里的延误险，或是藏在五层菜单深处的自动续费关闭入口。
但传统的「暗黑模式」再怎么狡猾，好歹还停留在视觉与认知博弈的层面。它给你设了套，但只要打起十二分精神，依然保有「选对或选错」的权利。
「摇一摇」之所以比以往任何广告都更招人厌恶，是因为它把这些毫无主观意图的自然物理动作，强行翻译成「我想去逛淘宝/京东」的商业指令。它已经不再是让你不小心「选错」，而是从物理层面上剥夺了你「不选」的权利。
把用户的一次抬手、一次转身，甚至只是想跳过广告的动作当成流量提款机，这种彻底越界的傲慢，才是摇一摇跳转真正令人深恶痛绝的原因。
这回，苹果真得抄安卓作业
虽然苹果上线「限制动作数据」值得给个好评，但客观来说，苹果在这场防跳转保卫战里，算是一个迟到了两年的「补课生」。
早在 2023 年前后，每天直接与本土流氓软件贴身肉搏的国产安卓厂商，就已经在各自的定制系统里针对「摇一摇」筑起了高墙。而且在权限的精细程度上，不少安卓系统其实比今天刚交卷的 iOS 27.2 考虑得更加周全。
最典型的差距就在于前面提到的「导航误伤」问题。
而国产安卓阵营早就洞察到了这个痛点，发明出了一个极其聪明的权限档位——「仅开屏时拒绝」。过去进入软件主界面后，系统再自动放开传感器权限，完全不影响你正常用看地图、或者在软件里摇一摇。
我们也整理了现有的主流安卓与鸿蒙机型，整理在最新系统下能否打开相关的设置以及设置的路径：
但即便如此，苹果在 iOS 27.2 正式版中亲自下场，依然是一个极具分量的转折点。
当 iOS 和安卓两大操作系统在底层逻辑上完成合围，那个靠调高陀螺仪灵敏度、把用户的每一次手抖都当成流量的「摇一摇」荒诞时代，也是时候彻底翻篇了。
今晚给 iPhone 升个级，把那几个让你烦了三年的手机 App 拉进黑名单吧。

According to Apple's tech specs page, the option for 16GB of unified memory remains limited to 153GB/s. That's identical to the M5 version, while only the new 24GB and 32GB configurations receive the faster 170GB/s memory bandwidth. For comparison, the high-end MacBook Pro with M5 Pro chip offers 307GB/s memory bandwidth, and the high-end model with the M5 Max features up to 614GB/s memory bandwidth. Pricing starts at $1,999, with 16GB of unified memory and 1TB of storage as standard. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro is available in Space Black and Silver, with configurations up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage. The new MacBook Pro is available to pre-order from Wednesday ahead of a November 6 launch. units.text: The lower-end 14-inch MacBook Pro got an update on Tuesday, with the model getting better wireless networking, and most importantly, more power with the M6 processor.
It's not the flashiest of upgrades, nor is there an associated enclosure re-design. But, in the middle of a week of upgrades, Apple announced the new model in a press release.
There's still no M6 Pro or M6 Max processor, and those are not expected soon, if ever. However, the "entry level" MacBook Pro is getting the M6 chip that debuted in the Mac mini.
The M6 processor here has 12 processing cores broken down into two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. The M6 here also has 12 GPU cores.
It comes standard with 16GB of RAM. Thunderbolt 4 remains.
Apple also says that the battery life has been extended to up to 14 hours of use.

Along with that, Apple's N1 chip is included. That incorporates Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. And, as before, Apple claims that improves performance and reliability of AirDrop and other wireless connectivity features.

"The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device," said Shelly Goldberg, Apple's vice president of Hardware Engineering. "With the powerful M6 chip, we're taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value."
Apple's performance testing
The company also has something to say about performance versus prior generations. Take these with a grain of salt, as always.
Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Preorder timing and cost
Prices start at $1999 with the M6, 1TB of storage, and 16GB of RAM. There is only one M6 chip to pick from, but with 32GB of RAM and a 4TB SSD, the new model sells for $3899.
Preorders start on October 28, with models expected to arrive on November 6.

The M6 processor here has 12 processing cores broken down into two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. The M6 here also has 12 GPU cores.
It comes standard with 16GB of RAM. Thunderbolt 4 remains.
Apple also says that the battery life has been extended to up to 14 hours of use.

Along with that, Apple's N1 chip is included. That incorporates Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. And, as before, Apple claims that improves performance and reliability of AirDrop and other wireless connectivity features.
Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.
Prices start at $1999 with the M6, 1TB of storage, and 16GB of RAM. There is only one M6 chip to pick from, but with 32GB of RAM and a 4TB SSD, the new model sells for $3899.
Preorders start on October 28, with models expected to arrive on November 6.
